subject: On-prem cluster preflight: vendor-locked provisioning & evacuation plan
messages:
From: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@blueridge-systems.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem cluster preflight: vendor-locked provisioning & evacuation plan

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we discussed, BlueRidge is preparing a vendor-locked on-prem rollout (locked BMC/boot firmware, restricted egress) and we need Redwood's preflight guidance: provisioning approach, nodeclass mix for GPUs + storage-heavy tenants, and an evacuation plan in the event of a hardware failure or vendor lockdown.

Key constraints:
- Vendor images are signed and require offline imaging process (no cloud imaging agent).
- Nodes will be a heterogeneous mix: 2x GPU nodes (A100 equiv), 8x CPU-only nodes per rack, attached NVMe for local cache and blockstore for persistent layers.
- Strict egress policy: only specific IPs allowed via a NAT gateway in our DMZ.
- Legal asks that PV encryption keys be rotated quarterly and access audited.

Can you send a short operational plan (preflight checks, evacuation playbook, and recommended PV rotation cadence) and let us know what we need from the vendor (console access, offline imaging media, HSM/KMS endpoints)? We'd like to validate this with our security and legal teams this month.

Attachments: vendor-network-diagram-v1.png (image/png)

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Jenkins
Director, Infrastructure — BlueRidge Systems
ben.jenkins@blueridge-systems.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@blueridge-systems.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster preflight: vendor-locked provisioning & evacuation plan

On Tue, Aug 17, 2026 at 9:12 AM Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@blueridge-systems.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the walkthrough last week...

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. High level we can support the constraints you listed; below is a concise preflight + immediate asks so we can produce a runbook for legal/security review.

Redwood proposed preflight checklist (short):
- Inventory: node hardware types + serials, NIC mappings, NVMe mapping to OS (device names), and BIOS/BMC access policy.
- Imaging: vendor-signed offline image ingestion steps (we can provide an ISO-based agent you run locally) and verification (SHA256) procedure.
- Networking: list of required outbound endpoints (IPs/FQDNs) for control plane, telemetry, and package pulls; NAT hole punching policy for our control plane reachability.
- PV/Encryption: recommended PV classes (blockstore for long-term, local SSD for cache), KMS/HSM integration points; quarterly key rotation cadence + audit hooks.
- Evacuation: canary/maintenance flows (drain, migrate cache, attach PV to fallback nodes), and fallback model variants for degraded hardware (smaller batch sizes).

Immediate asks for BlueRidge team:
1) Confirm whether vendor will provide HSM/KMS or if you will provide a reachable key-wrapping endpoint (we need url and auth method).
2) Confirm outbound whitelist will allow these IPs: 34.201.12.45, 54.86.33.21, and api.redwood.com (we'll provide final list).
3) Share node inventory CSV and the network diagram in full-resolution.

I've attached a short preflight checklist (redwood_preflight_checklist.xlsx) and a proposed timeline. Rishi will draft the PV rotation proposal and runbook; Lauren will validate network requirements with your infra team.

Propose a 60-minute preflight call on Thu Aug 20 at 10:00am PT to walk the runbook. Does that work?

Attachments: redwood_preflight_checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@blueridge-systems.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: SLA-legal <legal@blueridge-systems.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster preflight: vendor-locked provisioning & evacuation plan

Marissa — good checklist. A few clarifications from our side after vendor sync: 
- Vendor will supply signed images and an imaging console. They are not exposing BMC to third parties; imaging will be run by our datacenter ops team. We'll provide the signed media and a hash.
- HSM: vendor offers a local HSM appliance with an admin interface on a management VLAN. They can export wrapped keys to an external KMS when requested, but they won't host a public endpoint.
- Network: we can open the outbound list you provided to a NAT in our DMZ, plus we'll allow api.redwood.com (we can add the specific IPs once you confirm).
- Node mix: per rack: 2x gpu (A100 equiv) + 8x cpu-only. For the first canary we'd like 1 GPU + 4 CPU nodes.

We're attaching a short PV/key rotation proposal that our security team drafted — they want quarterly rotation but are open to Redwood's recommended steps to minimize downtime. Also attached the full-res network diagram.

Attachments: pv-key-rotation-proposal.pdf (application/pdf), vendor-network-diagram-v1-full.png (image/png)

Can we scope the evacuation playbook to handle a "vendor lockdown" scenario: if the vendor denies console access to a failed node, we need documented steps to failover workloads and recover PVs to alternate hosts. That is the primary ask from our security team.

Thanks,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jenkins <ben.jenkins@blueridge-systems.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-19T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem cluster preflight: vendor-locked provisioning & evacuation plan

Ben — appreciate the details and the attachments. Summary and next steps below so legal/security have a clear artifact.

Confirmed scope (what Redwood will deliver before the preflight call):
- Runbook: step-by-step offline imaging verification, node enrollment, and SHA256 verification for vendor-signed images.
- Evacuation playbook: two-tier strategy:
  1) Normal failure (console accessible): drain -> live-migrate/cache-flush -> reattach PVs -> reprovision node.
  2) Vendor-lockdown (console not accessible): mark node unschedulable, detach local caches, failover PV mounts to fallback blockstore (we'll provide automation to rebind PVCs to fallback PVs in your blockstore), and shift traffic to canary model variants.
- PV key rotation: Rishi will produce a key-rotation sequence that leverages the vendor HSM for root wrapping; Redwood will orchestrate rewrapping and re-encrypting PVs without application downtime when possible (we'll do staged rotations with rolling re-mounts).

Action items (owners):
- Ben / BlueRidge: provide node inventory CSV and vendor imaging media hashes (by 2026-08-21).
- Rishi (redwood): draft PV rotation playbook + automation hooks (delivery 2026-08-24).
- Lauren (redwood): produce exact outbound IP/FQDN list and network peering checklist (delivery 2026-08-21).
- Marissa (redwood): compile final preflight deck and send to legal/security for review (delivery 2026-08-21).

Proposed timeline:
- Mon Aug 24: internal dry run of evacuation playbook with simulated vendor-lockdown (redwood infra).
- Thu Aug 27: joint preflight call (60m) to walk runbook and confirm roles.

If that looks good, I'll schedule the Thu Aug 27 slot and share the invite + drive folder with the artifacts.

Attachments referenced: redwood_preflight_checklist.xlsx; pv-key-rotation-proposal.pdf

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Strategic Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 650-555-0199
